question: Explain the principle of separate legal entity of a company and the circumstances in which the corporate veil may be lifted.
sources: Companies Act, 2013 (incorporation and separate legal entity of a company)
Salomon v A Salomon & Co Ltd (House of Lords, 1897) - separate legal entity
Doctrine of lifting the corporate veil as developed by courts and under the Companies Act, 2013

points.label: Separate legal entity
points.description: On incorporation a company becomes a legal person distinct from its members; it owns its property and is liable for its own debts, as settled in Salomon v Salomon & Co.
points.basis: Salomon v A Salomon & Co Ltd (1897); effect of incorporation under the Companies Act, 2013

points.label: Meaning of lifting the veil
points.description: Lifting the corporate veil means ignoring the separate personality of the company and looking at the persons behind it, holding them liable for its acts.
points.basis: Doctrine of lifting the corporate veil (judicial principle)

points.label: Fraud and improper conduct
points.description: Where the company form is used to commit fraud, evade an existing legal obligation or carry on improper conduct, courts may disregard it.
points.basis: Judicial grounds for lifting the corporate veil: fraud or improper conduct

points.label: Tax evasion and enemy character
points.description: Courts may lift the veil to prevent evasion of tax or protect revenue, and to find out whether a company has enemy character from the nationality of those in control.
points.basis: Judicial grounds for lifting the corporate veil: protection of revenue; determination of enemy character

points.label: Statutory instances
points.description: The Companies Act itself makes directors or officers personally liable in some cases, for example for fraudulent conduct of business or for misstatements in a prospectus.
points.basis: Companies Act, 2013, provisions imposing personal liability on officers for fraud and misstatement
